install "docker compose" in the Dockerimage. right now it gives ╰─$ docker compose
docker: unknown command: docker compose
Let me look at the Dockerfile first to understand the current setup.
{"pattern": "Dockerfile*"}
{"filePath": "/home/user/project/Dockerfile"}

The issue is clear. The Dockerfile installs `docker-compose` (the old standalone v1 Python binary) and `docker.io`, but `docker compose` (v2) is a Docker CLI plugin that needs to be installed differently.

The fix is to replace `docker-compose` with `docker-compose-plugin` in the apt package list, which provides the `docker compose` subcommand.
{"filePath": "/home/user/project/Dockerfile", "oldString": "    docker-compose \\\n    docker.io \\", "newString": "    docker-compose-plugin \\\n    docker.io \\"}

The change replaces `docker-compose` (v1 standalone binary, invoked as `docker-compose`) with `docker-compose-plugin` (v2 CLI plugin, invoked as `docker compose`). The plugin integrates with the Docker CLI so `docker compose` works as a subcommand.

rows.content: `docker-compose-plugin` is only available from Docker's official apt repository, not Ubuntu's default repos. I need to add the Docker apt repo and install from there. The Dockerfile already installs `docker.io` from Ubuntu's repo — I'll switch both to the official Docker packages.
{"filePath": "/home/user/project/Dockerfile", "oldString": "    docker-compose-plugin \\\n    docker.io \\", "newString": "    docker-ce-cli \\\n    docker-compose-plugin \\"}
Now add the Docker official apt repo setup before the main apt-get install block:

{"filePath": "/home/user/project/Dockerfile", "oldString": "USER root
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \", "newString": "USER root
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Add Docker's official apt repository for docker-ce-cli and docker-compose-plugin
RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl gnupg \
    && install -m 0755 -d /etc/apt/keyrings \
    && curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg -o /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc \
    && chmod a+r /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc \
    && echo "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc] https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu $(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_CODENAME") stable" \
       > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.list \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \"}

Build succeeded on the first try. Here's what was changed:

- Added a new `RUN` step before the main package install that adds Docker's official apt repository (key + sources list entry)
- Replaced `docker.io` + `docker-compose` (Ubuntu's old packages) with `docker-ce-cli` + `docker-compose-plugin` (Docker's official packages)

`docker compose` (v2 plugin) is now available in the image.
